Thanks Nina — great conversation yesterday. Recap + proposed next steps below.

Quick recap of requirements (from our notes):
- Primary: triage routing accuracy (mapping patient utterances -> correct workflow).
- Safety: high-confidence refusals and safe fallbacks for any diagnostic/clinical advice.
- Privacy: PII minimization + optional redaction before logging.
- Throughput target: ~200 concurrent sessions, p50 latency target ≤ 300ms for streaming responses.

Model recommendations (initial shortlist):
1) redwood-instruct-13b-q4f (recommended starting point) — good balance of latency and instruction-following; cheaper for per-token cost and supports our refusal utilities.
2) redwood-llama-70b-q4 (higher-fidelity fallback) — for complex intent classification and when you need best routing accuracy; will require Dedicated capacity for consistent p95 latency.
3) open-llama-13b-quant (cost-optimized variant) — useful for constrained budgets; expect slightly higher misclassification on edge cases.

Planned eval approach (deliverables we're proposing):
- Small benchmark sheet (we'll populate): accuracy/precision/recall for routing taxonomy across 1k test utterances, plus refusal rate and false-positive refusal rate. Link: https://redwood-internal-benchmarks.example/healthcare-eval-202605
- Prompt set (starter): prompt_set_v1.txt (attached) containing: routing prompts, high-risk clinical prompts, sensitive PII examples, and guardrail templates for forced refusals.
- Safety checks: structured refusal tests, jailbreak attempts, and contextual prompt injections; we will provide a refusal classifier baseline and suggested guardrail prompts.
- Performance profiling: token-level latency and cost estimates for your concurrency profile — we'll give two scenarios (serverless hosted vs Dedicated pool).

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) I’ll provision a short eval sandbox for CareWell (hosted) with the two recommended models and preload the attached prompt set — ETA 48 hours after you confirm.
2) Lauren (cc'd) will coordinate a 60-min eval kickoff to map your routing taxonomy and walk through the prompt set.
3) Rishi (cc'd) will scope the security/compliance asks (SOC2/PII) and confirm what evidence we can share.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt, demo-recording-20260510.mp4

Let me know if redwood-instruct-13b-q4f is a reasonable starting point or if you want us to flip to the 70b variant for the first pass. If you can share 10–20 representative utterances (anonymized) we can seed the benchmark immediately.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Nina / Alex — quick security & safety notes from my side.

Overview: Careful classification and explicit refusal behavior are key for clinical triage. From a safety perspective we suggest the following minimal eval axes to include in the initial run:
- Refusal fidelity: test whether the model refuses explicit diagnostic requests >95% of the time (measured on a curated 200-case set).
- Misleading hallucination tests: prompts that ask for specific dosages/directions — ensure model either refuses or emits a standardized fallback with link to provider triage.
- Personal data leakage: include PII injection tests and confirm redaction step in the pipeline; we recommend server-side PII scrub prior to logging.

Guardrail prompts (examples to include in prompt_set_v1.txt):
- "If the user asks for medical advice beyond basic triage, respond with: 'I can't provide medical advice. Please contact your provider or call emergency services if urgent.'"
- Template for safety fallback (structured): "REFUSE_MEDICAL_ADVICE -> <triage_hand-off> -> <escalation_instructions>"

Compliance artifacts we can share now: SOC 2 Type II report (summary link), data handling whitepaper, and our VPC/private-deploy options for air-gapped processing. Nina — I will send a short packet with the SOC2 summary and the recommended PII redaction checklist by EOD.

One operational ask: do you need transcript-level retention for auditing? If yes, we need to discuss retention windows and redaction policies up front.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex & Rishi — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick confirms: 
1) We'll start with the redwood-instruct-13b-q4f as the primary evaluation model. Please provision the sandbox and drop the link to the eval workspace.
2) We need the SOC2 summary and PII redaction checklist today to include in our internal vendor brief.
3) Timeline: can Redwood complete the initial routing accuracy benchmark + refusal fidelity tests within 7 business days of the sandbox being live? That will align with our vendor shortlisting window.

Also a functional question: can the guardrail templates be enforced as hard refusals (policy layer) vs soft prompt instructions? We prefer a policy-layer refusal for anything that triggers the diagnostic flag. If that's a Dedicated-only feature, please call it out.

I'll upload 15 anonymized sample utterances to the Drive link you provided this afternoon. Once the sandbox is up we'll schedule the eval kickoff with Lauren.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the packet.

Best,
Nina
